claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A physics-informed reduced-order multiscale simulation coupling RVE models with machine-learning surrogates can predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed framework will be more accurate than conventional first-principles, CALPHAD, and standard machine-learning methods.
The proposed framework will be more computationally efficient than conventional first-principles, CALPHAD, and standard machine-learning methods.
Reduced-order RVE simulations can bypass computationally intensive full-scale ab initio calculations.
An RVE can represent the localized heterogeneities in the hierarchical microstructure.
Localized microstructural heterogeneities influence the alloy’s macroscopic mechanical behavior.
Physics-based constraints and microstructural simulation data narrow the machine-learning model’s solution space.
Narrowing the solution space improves predictions of elastic modulus, yield point, and fracture toughness.
Use of a surrogate model significantly reduces computation time relative to full first-principles or CALPHAD approaches.
Prior methods have approximately 20% relative prediction error.
The proposed method is expected to achieve approximately 10–12% relative error for Young’s modulus.
The proposed method is expected to achieve approximately 10–12% relative error for yield strength.
The proposed method is expected to provide a comparable improvement for toughness prediction.
The proposed method is expected to be at least five times as computationally efficient as full-scale simulations.
Existing first-principles, CALPHAD, and unmodified machine-learning methods have high computational demands.
Existing methods have only moderate predictive accuracy, particularly for toughness.
The method may lose reliability when processing variations significantly alter the hierarchical microstructure.
The method may lose reliability when environmental degradation or unmodeled toughening mechanisms dominate.
The method may lose reliability when local heterogeneities exceed the representational capacity of the selected RVEs.

contradictions.description: The expected Young’s-modulus and yield-strength errors are stated as 10–12%, but the hypothesis is declared falsified if either error exceeds 10%. Thus part of the predicted range would itself trigger falsification.
